pages.title: House Cleaning Price Calculator: Price Every Clean So It Pays You | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free house cleaning price calculator. Enter your pay goal, hours and costs to get your break-even rate, your target rate and a quote for any clean, drive time included.
pages.lede: Find what a clean has to cost so it pays you: your break-even rate, your target rate and a quote for the job, with drive time and self-employment tax counted. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Break-even rate, target rate and a quote for any clean, drive time included.
pages.costs_hint: Insurance, phone, apps, marketing, equipment, fees
method: Most cleaners divide the pay they want by the hours they work. That leaves out three things: the hours nobody pays for (driving, quoting, invoicing), the business costs that run every month, and self-employment tax.

This calculator grosses your take-home up for self-employment tax (15.3% on 92.35% of profit) and your income tax estimate, adds a year of business costs, and spreads the total over the hours customers actually pay for. That is your break-even rate. Your margin on top gives the target rate.
A job's price floor is your time on site and your drive time at the break-even rate, plus vehicle cost per mile and supplies. The quote adds your margin and rounds up to the next $5.
pages.example: A $52,000 take-home goal with a 12% income tax estimate needs $70,394 of profit before tax. Add $6,540 a year of business costs and you need $76,934 of revenue. At 48 weeks of 45 hours with 65% paid, that is 1,404 paid hours: a break-even rate of $54.80 and a target of $64.47 with a 15% margin. Pay divided by all hours would say $24.07. A standard 2-bed clean (2.5 hours on site, a 15-mile round trip, $8 of supplies) has a $183.79 price floor and quotes at $220, with $36.21 of profit inside it.

faq: How much should I charge to clean a house?

There is no single right price, because it depends on your pay goal, your costs and how many of your hours customers pay for. Enter yours above and the calculator shows the lowest price that covers them and a quote with your margin.
Why is my break-even rate so much higher than my pay divided by my hours?

Because part of every week is unpaid (driving, quoting, admin), your business costs keep running, and as a self-employed cleaner you pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare. Each of those raises the rate every paid hour has to carry.
Does it work for deep cleans and move-outs?
Yes. Pick an example job or type your own hours, crew size, supplies and miles. The example jobs are starting points, not market prices.
Is this tax advice?
No. It is a planning estimate. Ask your tax preparer for your real income tax rate.
pages.sources: Self-employment tax: 15.3% on 92.35% of net profit (IRS Topic 554, Schedule SE). Vehicle: IRS business mileage rate 76 cents a mile for July 1 to December 31, 2026 (IRS news release IR-2026-29). Checked Oct 6, 2026.

faq: How much should I charge to pressure wash a driveway?
It depends on your pay goal, costs and travel. With the example numbers a 2-car concrete driveway needs $200 to pay its share; enter your own numbers to see yours.
Should I price by the square foot or by the hour?
Square-foot prices hide how long a job takes you. This calculator prices from time, crew, supplies and travel; for square-foot pricing, enter the hours a job of that size takes you.
Does it handle two-person jobs?
Yes. Set people on the job to 2 and both people's time on site and drive time are counted.

pages.title: Hourly Rate Calculator for Freelancers and Self-Employed | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free hourly rate calculator. Enter the take-home pay you want, your tax set-aside, expenses and billable hours to get your minimum hourly rate, and test any rate before you quote it.
pages.lede: Find the hourly rate that pays you what you want after tax and costs, then test any rate before you quote it. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Your minimum hourly rate, and what any rate really pays you.
method: Your take-home is grossed up for the tax you set aside, then a year of business expenses is added. That is the revenue you need.
Spread that revenue over the hours a client actually pays for (your working hours times your billable share) and you have your minimum hourly rate. The rate card rounds it up to the next $5.
To test a rate, the calculator multiplies it by your billable hours, takes out expenses and your tax set-aside on any profit, and divides what is left by every hour you work.
pages.example: A $60,000 take-home with a 25% tax set-aside and $6,000 of expenses needs $86,000 of revenue. At 48 weeks of 40 hours with 60% billable, that is 1,152 billable hours, so the minimum rate is $74.65 (rate card $75). Charging $40 an hour brings in $46,080 and leaves $30,060 after expenses and tax: $15.66 for every hour worked, $29,940 short of the goal.

cta.title: Keep it, change it, quote with it
bullets: The Hourly Rate Quick Calculator is this calculator as a one-tab Excel and Google Sheets workbook,
with a job quote section, a rate card and a Start Here guide. $2.99, instant download.

faq: How do I calculate my hourly rate as a freelancer?
Start from the take-home you want, add the tax you set aside and your business expenses, then divide by the hours clients actually pay for, not every hour you work.
What share of my hours is billable?
Many self-employed people bill 50% to 70% of their working hours; the rest goes to admin, sales and travel. Track a few weeks to find yours.
What tax set-aside rate should I use?
Ask your tax preparer. A set-aside rate is a savings habit, not a tax calculation.
Is this tax advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.
pages.sources: Tax set-aside is your own estimate; ask your tax preparer. Checked Oct 6, 2026.

pages.title: 13 Week Cash Flow Calculator for Ecommerce | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free 13 week cash flow calculator for ecommerce brands. Enter cash today, weekly payouts, weekly costs and one purchase order to see your lowest cash week and the cash you need to cover it.
pages.h1: 13 Week Cash Flow Calculator for Ecommerce
pages.lede: See the week your cash bottoms out and how much you need to cover it, before a purchase order lands. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Your lowest cash week in the next 13, and the cash needed to cover it.
method: Each week starts with last week's ending cash, adds the payouts that reach your bank and takes out your fixed costs and ad spend. In the week the purchase order is due, its payment comes out too.
The lowest ending cash across the 13 weeks is your low point. If it is below zero, the cash needed is the amount that keeps that week at zero.

This free version uses one weekly figure for cash in and one purchase order paid in a single week. Real brands wait days or weeks for each channel to pay out and pay POs as a deposit and a balance; the full workbook models both.
pages.example: Say a brand starts with $20,000 and collects $53,700 a week after fees while paying $32,000 a week in payroll, fixed costs and ads. That adds $21,700 a week, so cash reaches $85,100 by week 3. A $117,000 PO balance due in week 4 takes it to -$10,200, so the brand needs $10,200 more by then, or a later due date. By week 13 cash is back to $185,100. The weekly figures are the week 1 numbers from example 1 of the 13-Week E-commerce Cash Flow workbook; the starting cash and due week are changed to show a squeeze.

cta.title: The full 13-week cash flow
bullets: The 13-Week E-commerce Cash Flow workbook models each channel's payout lag (Amazon, TikTok Shop, your own store, retail), six POs as deposit plus balance and freight,
factoring cost in dollars, a credit line, side-by-side scenarios and a PO planner, for Excel and Google Sheets.

faq: What is a 13 week cash flow?
A week-by-week plan of the cash coming in and going out over the next quarter, so you can see the lowest week before it happens. Thirteen weeks is one quarter.
Why can a profitable store run out of cash?
Sales are recorded when they happen, but payouts arrive later and inventory is paid for before it sells. Growing sales and big purchase orders widen that gap.
Should I use sales or payouts for cash in?
Payouts: the money that reaches your bank after fees and refunds, in the week it arrives.
What if the lowest week is below zero?
You need that much cash, credit or a later payment date by that week. Moving a PO's due date is often the first lever to test.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.
pages.sources: No rates or fees are assumed: every figure is yours. Page checked Oct 7, 2026.
